sentences.en: Models for arguments.
sentences.zh: 论证的模式。
sentences.asr_text: Models for arguments.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: Good morning, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: My name is David and I am good at arguing.
sentences.zh: 我叫戴维，我很擅长辩论。

sentences.en: So welcome to our introductory lecture on argumentation.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到我们的论证学入门讲座。

sentences.en: Why do we want to argue?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么想要争辩呢？

sentences.en: Why do we try to convince other people to believe things that they don’t want to believe?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要设法说服别人相信他们原本不愿相信的事情？

sentences.en: And is that even a nice thing to do?
sentences.zh: 而且，这样做真的好吗？

sentences.en: Is that a nice way to treat other human beings, try and make them think something they don’t want to think?
sentences.zh: 设法让别人去想他们原本不愿想的事情，这样对待他人算友善吗？

sentences.en: Well, my answer is going to make reference to three models for arguments.
sentences.zh: 我的回答会涉及三种论证模式。

sentences.en: The first model—let’s call this the dialectical model—is that we think of arguments as war.
sentences.zh: 第一种模式，我们姑且称之为辩证模式，就是把论证看成战争。

sentences.en: And you know what that’s like.
sentences.zh: 你们知道那是什么样的。

sentences.en: There is a lot of screaming and shouting and winning and losing.
sentences.zh: 其中充斥着尖叫、大喊，以及输赢之争。

sentences.en: And that’s not really a very helpful model for arguing, but it’s a pretty common and fixed one.
sentences.zh: 这其实不是一种很有帮助的论证模式，但它确实相当常见，而且根深蒂固。

sentences.en: I guess you must have seen that type of arguing many times—in the street, on the bus or in the subway.
sentences.zh: 我想，你们一定在街上、公交车上或地铁里，见过很多次这样的争吵。

sentences.en: Let’s move on to the second model.
sentences.zh: 我们接着来看第二种模式。

sentences.en: The second model for arguing regards arguments as proofs.
sentences.zh: 第二种论证模式把论证看成证明。

sentences.en: Think of a mathematician’s argument.
sentences.zh: 想一想数学家的论证。

sentences.en: Here’s my argument.
sentences.zh: 这是我的论证。

sentences.en: Does it work?
sentences.zh: 它成立吗？

sentences.en: Is it any good?
sentences.zh: 它是否合理？

sentences.en: Are the premises warranted?
sentences.zh: 这些前提有充分根据吗？

sentences.en: Are the inferences valid?
sentences.zh: 这些推理有效吗？

sentences.en: Does the conclusion follow the premises?
sentences.zh: 结论能从前提中推导出来吗？

sentences.en: No opposition, no adversariality—not necessarily any arguing in the adversarial sense.
sentences.zh: 这里没有对立，也没有敌对，并不一定涉及敌对意义上的争辩。

sentences.en: And there’s a third model to keep in mind that I think is going to be very helpful, and that is arguments as performances, arguments as being in front of an audience.
sentences.zh: 还有第三种值得记住的模式，我认为它会很有用：把论证看成表演，也就是在听众面前展开论证。

sentences.en: We can think of a politician trying to present a position, trying to convince the audience of something.
sentences.zh: 可以想象一位政治人物试图阐明某种立场，并说服听众接受它。

sentences.en: But there’s another twist on this model that I really think is important; namely, that when we argue before an audience, sometimes the audience has a more participatory role in the argument; that is, you present your arguments in front of an audience who are like juries that make a judgment and decide the case.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为这种模式还有一个重要的变体：在听众面前论证时，听众有时会更多地参与进来；也就是说，听众就像陪审团，会作出判断并裁决结果。

sentences.en: Let’s call this model the rhetorical model, where you have to tailor your argument to the audience at hand.
sentences.zh: 我们把这种模式称为修辞模式，在这种模式中，你必须根据眼前的听众调整论证。

sentences.en: Of those three, the argument as war is the dominant one.
sentences.zh: 在这三种模式中，把论证视为战争的模式占据主导地位。

sentences.en: It dominates how we talk about arguments, it dominates how we think about arguments, and because of that, it shapes how we argue, our actual conduct in arguments.
sentences.zh: 它支配着我们谈论论证和思考论证的方式，因此也塑造了我们如何论证，以及我们在论证中的实际行为。

sentences.en: We want strong arguments, arguments that have a lot of punch, arguments that are right on target.
sentences.zh: 我们想要强有力、冲击力十足、一针见血的论点。

sentences.en: We want to have our defenses up and our strategies all in order.
sentences.zh: 我们希望做好防守，安排好所有策略。

sentences.en: We want killer arguments.
sentences.zh: 我们想要能一击制胜的论点。

w.m: adj.极有杀伤力的；极有说服力的

sentences.en: That’s the kind of argument we want.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们想要的那种论证。

sentences.en: It is the dominant way of thinking about arguments.
sentences.zh: 这是思考论证时占主导地位的方式。

sentences.en: When I’m talking about arguments, that’s probably what you thought of, the adversarial model.
sentences.zh: 我一谈到论证，你们想到的大概就是这种对抗模式。

sentences.en: But the war metaphor, the war paradigm or model for thinking about arguments, has, I think, negative effects on how we argue.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，战争这个隐喻，也就是用来思考论证的战争范式或模式，会对我们的论证方式产生负面影响。

sentences.en: First, it elevates tactics over substance.
sentences.zh: 首先，它把策略置于实质内容之上。

sentences.en: You can take a class in logic argumentation.
sentences.zh: 你可以去上一门逻辑论证课程。

sentences.en: You learn all about the strategies that people use to try and win arguments and it makes arguing adversarial; it’s polarizing.
sentences.zh: 你会学到人们试图赢得论战时使用的各种策略，而这让论证变得具有对抗性，使人们走向两极。

sentences.en: And the only foreseeable outcomes are triumph—glorious triumph—or disgraceful defeat.
sentences.zh: 唯一可以预见的结果，就是胜利，辉煌的胜利，或是耻辱的失败。

sentences.en: I think those are very destructive effects, and worst of all, it seems to prevent things like negotiation and collaboration.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些影响极具破坏性；更糟的是，这种模式似乎会阻碍协商与合作之类的事情。

sentences.en: I think the argument-as-a-war metaphor inhibits those other kinds of resolutions to argumentation.
sentences.zh: 我认为，把论证视为战争的隐喻，会抑制其他解决争论的方式。

sentences.en: And finally—this is really the worst thing—arguments don’t seem to get us anywhere; they’re dead ends.
sentences.zh: 最后，也是最糟的一点，争论似乎让我们毫无进展，走进了死胡同。

w.m: phr.死胡同；没有出路的局面

sentences.en: We don’t get anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我们没有取得任何进展。

sentences.en: Oh, and one more thing.
sentences.zh: 哦，还有一件事。

sentences.en: That is, if argument is war, then there’s also an implicit aspect of meaning—learning with losing.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果论证就是战争，那么其中还暗含着另一层意义：在失败中学习。

sentences.en: And let me explain what I mean.
sentences.zh: 让我解释一下我的意思。

sentences.en: Suppose you and I have an argument.
sentences.zh: 假设你和我展开一场争论。

sentences.en: You believe a proposition and I don’t.
sentences.zh: 你相信某个命题，而我不相信。

sentences.en: And I say, “Well, why do you believe that?”
sentences.zh: 我问你：“你为什么相信它呢？”

sentences.en: And you give me your reasons.
sentences.zh: 于是你给出了你的理由。

sentences.en: And I object and say, “Well, what about...?”
sentences.zh: 我表示反对，并问：“那么……又怎么解释呢？”

sentences.en: And you answer my objection.
sentences.zh: 你回应了我的异议。

sentences.en: And I have a question: “Well, what do you mean? How does it apply over here?”
sentences.zh: 接着我又有问题：“你是什么意思？这又怎么适用于这里呢？”

sentences.en: And you answer my question.
sentences.zh: 你又回答了我的问题。

sentences.en: Now, suppose at the end of the day, I’ve objected, I’ve questioned, I’ve raised all sorts of questions from an opposite perspective and in every case you’ve responded to my satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 现在，假设到最后，我已经提出过异议、追问过问题、从相反的角度提出过种种疑问，而每次你都给出了让我满意的回应。

sentences.en: And so at the end of the day, I say, “You know what? I guess you’re right.”
sentences.zh: 最后我说：“你知道吗？我想你是对的。”

sentences.en: Maybe finally I lost my argument.
sentences.zh: 也许最终是我输掉了这场争论。

sentences.en: But isn’t it also a process of learning?
sentences.zh: 但这不也是一个学习的过程吗？

sentences.en: So you see arguments may also have positive effects.
sentences.zh: 所以你们看，论证也可能产生积极影响。

sentences.en: So, how can we find new ways to achieve those positive effects?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们怎样才能找到实现这些积极影响的新方式呢？

sentences.en: We need to think of new kinds of arguments.
sentences.zh: 我们需要思考新类型的论证。

sentences.en: Here I have some suggestions.
sentences.zh: 我有一些建议。

sentences.en: If we want to think of new kinds of arguments, what we need to do is think of new kinds of arguers—people who argue.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想思考新类型的论证，就需要思考新类型的论辩者，也就是参与论辩的人。

sentences.en: So try this: Think of all the roles that people play in arguments.
sentences.zh: 不妨试一试：想想人们在论证中扮演的所有角色。

sentences.en: There’s the proponent and the opponent in an adversarial, dialectical argument.
sentences.zh: 在对抗性的辩证论证中，有提出主张的人和反对主张的人。

sentences.en: There’s the audience in rhetorical arguments.
sentences.zh: 在修辞论证中，有听众。

sentences.en: There’s the reasoner in arguments as proofs.
sentences.zh: 在作为证明的论证中，有进行推理的人。

sentences.en: All these different roles.
sentences.zh: 这些都是不同的角色。

sentences.en: Now, can you imagine an argument in which you are the arguer, but you’re also in the audience, watching yourself argue?
sentences.zh: 现在，你能否想象这样一场论证：你既是论辩者，也是听众，在旁观看自己论辩？

sentences.en: Can you imagine yourself watching yourself argue?
sentences.zh: 你能想象自己旁观自己论辩的样子吗？

sentences.en: That means you need to be supported by yourself.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你需要给自己支持。

sentences.en: Even when you lose the argument, still, at the end of the argument, you could say, “Wow, that was a good argument!”
sentences.zh: 即使输掉论证，到最后你仍然可以说：“哇，这真是一场精彩的论证！”

sentences.en: Can you do that?
sentences.zh: 你能做到吗？

sentences.en: I think you can.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以。

sentences.en: In this way, you’ve been supported by yourself.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，你就给了自己支持。

sentences.en: Up till now, I have lost a lot of arguments.
sentences.zh: 到现在为止，我已经输掉过很多次争论。

sentences.en: It really takes practice to become a good arguer, in the sense of being able to benefit from losing, but fortunately, I’ve had many, many colleagues who have been willing to step up and provide that practice for me.
sentences.zh: 要成为一个好的论辩者，能够从失败中获益，确实需要练习；幸运的是，我有许多同事愿意挺身而出，让我有机会练习。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: To sum up, in today’s lecture, I have introduced three models of arguments.
sentences.zh: 总结一下，在今天的讲座中，我介绍了三种论证模式。

sentences.en: The first model is called the dialectical model.
sentences.zh: 第一种叫作辩证模式。

sentences.en: The second one is the model of arguments as proofs.
sentences.zh: 第二种是把论证看成证明的模式。

sentences.en: And the last one is called the rhetorical model, the model of arguments as performances.
sentences.zh: 最后一种叫作修辞模式，也就是把论证看成表演的模式。

sentences.en: I have also emphasized that, though the adversarial type of arguments is quite common, we can still make arguments produce some positive effects.
sentences.zh: 我也强调了，虽然对抗式论证非常常见，但我们仍然可以让论证产生一些积极影响。

sentences.en: Next time I will continue our discussion on the process of arguing.
sentences.zh: 下次我会继续讨论论证的过程。

sentences.en: Now you have three minutes to check your work.
sentences.zh: 现在你有三分钟检查作答。

sentences.en: Good evening, everybody.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 各位晚上好。

sentences.en: Today we are pleased to have invited Maggie Shorts from Harvard University to tell us her feeling of studying together with her mom.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 今天我们很高兴邀请到哈佛大学的玛吉·肖茨，请她谈谈与妈妈一起上大学的感受。

sentences.en: Well, Maggie.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 那么，玛吉。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I’m very happy to meet you all.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到大家。

sentences.en: Maggie, are you and your mom studying the same major at the university?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 玛吉，你和妈妈在大学里学的是同一个专业吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 并不是。

sentences.en: She is studying in law school and I’m studying journalism.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 她在法学院读书，而我学的是新闻学。

sentences.en: So, you see she is a graduate student while I am an undergraduate.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 所以，她是研究生，而我是本科生。

sentences.en: Since we started at the same time and hers is a four-year night program, our school schedules are synched.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我们是同时开始上学的，而她读的是四年制夜校课程，所以我们的学习日程同步。

sentences.en: Which means?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 也就是说呢？

sentences.en: We follow the same schedule of study.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我们的学习日程安排是一样的。

sentences.en: We take our exams during the same busy weeks and experience similar relief at the end of December and May.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我们都在同样忙碌的几个星期里考试，也都在十二月和五月结束时如释重负。

sentences.en: Last spring, we compared notes on our cover letters and interviews for our job applications.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 去年春天，我们还交流了求职信和求职面试方面的心得。

sentences.en: Last June, as we were both preparing for our summer internships, my mother and I traded fashion advice.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 去年六月，我们都在准备暑期实习，妈妈和我还交换过穿搭建议。

sentences.en: Presently, we will probably graduate within days of each other.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 目前看来，我们毕业的日期可能只相差几天。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 真有意思。

sentences.en: Then you must have a lot in common at study.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 那么，你们在学习上一定有不少共同点。

sentences.en: You bet.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 那当然。

sentences.en: As students, we’ve shared study habits (take notes by hand), general truths (You can’t avoid having a few bad professors), and encouraging platitudes (like, it’s okay! No one will care how you did on your “Science of Cooking” or “Constitutional Law” midterm!).
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 作为学生，我们有共同的学习习惯，比如手写笔记；有共同的体会，比如难免会碰到几个不太好的教授；也会说些鼓励人的套话，比如“没关系，没人会在意你《烹饪科学》或《宪法学》期中考得怎么样！”

sentences.en: Where she’s listened to my complaints about freshman-year roommates and dining-hall food, I’ve helped her buy textbooks online and wished her luck in moot-court practice.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 她听我抱怨大一时的室友和食堂饭菜，我则帮她在网上买教材，还祝她模拟法庭练习顺利。

sentences.en: Occasionally, we’ve even studied together.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 有时我们甚至会一起学习。

sentences.en: When Mom came to visit during Freshman Parents Weekend, I took her into the library on the pretext that she was on a library tour.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 妈妈在大一新生家长周末来探望时，我以她在参观图书馆为由，带她进了图书馆。

sentences.en: We sat side by side in the big open room on the first floor—she diligently taking notes on a huge red volume that she had lugged from New York City on the train, I casually reading about Greek myths.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我们并排坐在一楼的大阅览室里：她认真记着笔记，读的是她从纽约坐火车费力带来的一本厚厚的红皮书；我则随意翻看希腊神话。

sentences.en: What do you think is the biggest advantage of having a parent studying together with you?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你觉得和父母一起上大学最大的好处是什么？

sentences.en: I know that my mother has felt the frustration of a paper that won’t write and the excitement of mastering a difficult topic.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我知道，妈妈也经历过论文写不出来的挫败感，以及攻克一个难题后的兴奋。

sentences.en: I don’t need to explain my elaborate theory that I am a “bad test-taker”—she said the same thing about herself.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我不必费心解释自己“不会考试”的那套复杂理论，因为她也这样说过自己。

sentences.en: And talking with her is a good way to get perspective on those occasional hurdles that crop up in college.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 和她聊聊天，能让我更理性地看待大学里偶尔出现的那些障碍。

sentences.en: Although we are both taking a substantial course load, Mom is also working a full-time job in the financial industry.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 虽然我们两个人的课业都很繁重，但妈妈同时还在金融行业做着一份全职工作。

sentences.en: That urges me to study harder, so I should say encouragement.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 这激励我更加努力地学习，所以我会说，最大的好处是受到鼓舞。

sentences.en: Any disadvantages then?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 那么，有什么不利之处吗？

sentences.en: Well, sometimes I wonder whether we are getting a little too involved in each other’s scholastic lives.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 有时候，我会想，我们是不是过多地介入了彼此的学业生活。

sentences.en: This usually occurs to me about twice a year, when my mother calls to inform me of her grades.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 通常每年大约有两次，妈妈打电话告诉我她的成绩时，我就会这样想。

sentences.en: Once, she reached me in the middle of a date (“I got my first A! Aren’t you going to congratulate me?”), and often, when the news has been disappointing, I haven’t known how to respond.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 有一次，她在我约会到一半时联系我，说“我第一次拿到A了！你不祝贺我一下吗？”而当她的成绩不理想时，我常常不知道该如何回应。

sentences.en: Last fall, I was chastised for passing along a speculative tidbit I had heard in the dining hall—that, because of grade inflation, GPAs once considered good might be viewed with new scrutiny.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 去年秋天，我把在食堂听到的一条未经证实的消息转告给她，结果受了责备：由于成绩膨胀，以前被认为不错的平均绩点，现在可能会受到更严格的审视。

sentences.en: “Jane has informed me that ’B is the new F,’” Mom announced at Thanksgiving.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 感恩节时，妈妈宣布：“简告诉我，现在的B就等于以前的F了。”

sentences.en: I didn’t know what to say to comfort her.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我不知道该说些什么来安慰她。

sentences.en: This is the end of part one of the interview.
sentences.zh: 访谈的第一部分到此结束。

sentences.en: Now listen to part two of the interview.
sentences.zh: 现在请听访谈的第二部分。
sentences.asr_text: Now listen to part two of the interview.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: Questions six to ten are based on part two of the interview.
sentences.zh: 第6至10题根据访谈的第二部分提问。
sentences.asr_text: Questions six to ten are based on part two of the interview.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: Is the phenomenon of parent and kids studying together at university a rare case?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 父母和孩子一起上大学，这种现象少见吗？

sentences.en: I am afraid not.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 恐怕并不少见。

sentences.en: Changing careers later in life is no longer a rarity, so it is not uncommon for students and their parents to be toying with the big decisions at the same time.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 在人生后期转行已经不是什么稀罕事了，因此，学生和父母同时考虑重大决定也并不少见。

sentences.en: Class surveys indicate that the majority of Harvard alumni have shifted directions when it comes to their careers.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 班级调查显示，大多数哈佛校友在职业发展中都曾改变方向。

sentences.en: With the financial collapse of 2008, such shifts have become more widespread.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 2008年金融危机之后，这种转变变得更加普遍。

sentences.en: Students have seen their family members lose jobs or change them.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 学生们见过家人失业或转行。

sentences.en: Gone is the time when you start out at a company and work there for the rest of your life.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 从进入一家公司起就在那儿工作一辈子的时代，已经过去了。

sentences.en: So your mom started study again just because she wanted to change her career?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 所以，你妈妈重新开始学习，就是因为她想转行吗？

sentences.en: Yes, she used to be in the real estate industry but now she wants to be a lawyer.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 是的，她以前从事房地产行业，现在则想成为一名律师。

sentences.en: Does her experience affect you somewhat?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 她的经历会对你产生一些影响吗？

sentences.en: Certainly.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Freshman Week, in one of the welcoming speeches, our dean mentioned that many of us might have grown up thinking that “doctor, lawyer, teacher” were our only options.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 新生周的一次欢迎致辞中，院长提到，我们很多人可能从小就认为“医生、律师、教师”是仅有的职业选择。

sentences.en: She urged us to stick to our dreams.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 她鼓励我们坚持自己的梦想。

sentences.en: But later I realized talking about passions is one thing—actually following them is another.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 但后来我意识到，谈论热爱的事情是一回事，真正去追随它们则是另一回事。

sentences.en: By the time I started to think about what professional directions I might want to take, I had heard “The average American changes careers seven times” so often that it was hard not to become numb to its message.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 当我开始思考自己可能会选择怎样的职业方向时，“美国人平均一生会转行七次”这句话我已经听得太多，几乎对此麻木了。

sentences.en: The last thing that the enthusiastic Harvard student wants to do is to imagine moving from job to job until she lands somewhere by chance, especially when the economy is so uncertain.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 一个满怀热情的哈佛学生，最不愿意想象的，就是自己在不同工作间辗转，直到碰巧落在某个岗位上，尤其是经济如此不确定的时候。

sentences.en: My mom can serve as a good example.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我妈妈就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Even if she graduated from Harvard herself as a brilliant student, she had to make alterations of her career.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 即使她当初也是以优异成绩从哈佛毕业，也仍然不得不调整自己的职业方向。

sentences.en: So, is your mom actually happy studying with younger students?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 那么，你妈妈和年轻学生一起上课，真的开心吗？

sentences.en: Hard to say.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 很难说。

sentences.en: Frustration is routine for older students, you know, who have to learn how to study all over again.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 对年长的学生来说，挫败感是家常便饭，因为他们得重新学会如何学习。

sentences.en: Mom once described the experience of taking classes with students half her age after 30 years in the workforce: “What’s most challenging is that you come into class knowing how to make a cake—but you’re all there to make omelets.”
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 妈妈曾这样描述自己工作三十年后，和年龄只有自己一半的学生一起上课的经历：“最有挑战的是，你走进教室时已经知道怎样做蛋糕了，但大家在这里学的却是做煎蛋卷。”

sentences.en: A kind of wasting time?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 有种在浪费时间的感觉？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Do you think your mom has played an important role in shaping your idea of what kind of person you want to be?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你觉得，在形成自己想成为什么样的人的观念时，妈妈发挥过重要作用吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Harvard offers many resources for students who want to figure out where their future lies.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 哈佛为想弄清未来方向的学生提供了许多资源。

sentences.en: Advisers, tutors, and OCS keep their doors open to help undergraduates embark on this kind of discovery.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 学业导师、辅导老师和职业服务办公室都敞开大门，帮助本科生开始这样的探索。

sentences.en: One can’t find one’s passions in a booklet on summer internships or a list of possible career paths.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 一个人无法仅凭一本暑期实习手册，或一张可能的职业道路清单，就找到自己的热爱。

sentences.en: It’s a gradual process that involves sharing thoughts and then coming back to them; a discussion that doesn’t always have its end goal in mind.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 这是一个循序渐进的过程，需要交流想法，再回过头来思考；这样的讨论并不总是一开始就有明确的终点。

sentences.en: In the course of my time at Harvard, it has been just such a give-and-take—with professors, with friends, and with my mother—that has slowly shaped my ideas of who I might want to be.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 在哈佛求学期间，正是和教授、朋友、妈妈之间这样的思想交流，慢慢塑造了我对未来想成为怎样的人的认识。

sentences.en: I really cherish the time she spent together with me at university.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我非常珍惜她和我一起在大学度过的时光。

sentences.en: Well, Maggie.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 好的，玛吉。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for staying with us today.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天和我们聊了这么多。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: This is the end of part two of the interview.
sentences.zh: 访谈的第二部分到此结束。
sentences.asr_text: This is the end of part two of the interview.

sentences.en: Question 6. Why is parent and kid studying together a common case?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第6题：为什么父母和孩子一起学习是一种常见现象？

sentences.en: Question 7. What would Maggie’s Mom like to be after college?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第7题：玛吉的妈妈大学毕业后想做什么？

sentences.en: Question 8. How does Maggie’s Mom feel about sitting in class after 30 years?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第8题：工作三十年后重返课堂，玛吉的妈妈有什么感受？

sentences.en: Question 9. What is most challenging for Maggie’s mom?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第9题：对玛吉的妈妈来说，最有挑战的是什么？

sentences.en: Question 10. How does Maggie describe the process of thinking out one’s career path?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第10题：玛吉如何描述探索自身职业道路的过程？
